stem: When does the most rapid proliferative growth phase of an infantile hemangioma usually occur?

options.text: During the third trimester of pregnancy.
In the first $3$ months of life.
In the first $48$ hours after delivery.

explanation: Rapid growth usually begins at $2$-$3$ weeks and is most intense during the first $3$ months, though it can continue up to $6$ months.
rationale: The proliferative phase starts a few weeks after birth and peaks within the first quarter of the first year.

optionExplanations.A: Hemangiomas are typically not present or are very subtle at birth; their growth happens postnatally.
optionExplanations.B: Rapid growth usually begins at $2$-$3$ weeks and is most intense during the first $3$ months, though it can continue up to $6$ months.
optionExplanations.C: By this age, most hemangiomas have reached their plateau or have already begun the slow process of involution.
optionExplanations.D: The source notes that at birth there is often nothing, and the rapid growth phase waits until the second or third week.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: In the first $3$ months of life.
